translations.text: Now, renowned man, search earnestly into spiritual mysteries with the power of your mind and the wisdom of your heart, so that you may truly know how it came about, when the Almighty was born through a pure virgin,

after he had chosen Mary, the finest of maidens, the glorious young woman, as his protection, that angels clothed in white garments did not appear there when the Prince came, the hero, into Bethlehem.
Messengers were ready, who then told the shepherds in spoken words and announced true joy: that the Son of the Lord had been born into the world, in Bethlehem.

Yet it does not say in the books that they appeared there in white garments at that noble time, as they did afterwards, when the glorious Lord, the majestic Prince, called his band of thegns, the beloved company, to Bethany.

On that day of joy they did not scorn the word of their teacher, their giver of treasure. At once they were ready, the men with their lord, for the holy city, where the giver of glory revealed many signs to them,
the protector of glory, in mysterious words, before the only-begotten Son, the co-eternal Child, ascended to his own Father, forty days by count after he had risen from death out of the earth.

Through his sufferings he had then fulfilled the words of the prophets throughout the world, as they had sung beforehand. The thegns praised and loved with joy the Lord of life, the Father of all creation.
Afterwards he gave his dear companions a fair reward for this, and the Ruler of angels, the mighty Lord, eager to go to his Father's kingdom, spoke these words: "Rejoice in your hearts!
I will never turn away from you. I will always keep my love for you, and give you power, and stay with you for ever and ever, so that through my grace you will never lack anything good.
Go now through all the vast earth, along the wide ways. Make it known to the multitudes, preach and proclaim the bright faith, and baptize the peoples under the heavens.
Turn to the heathens, destroy their idol-shrines, cast them down and hate them, put out enmity, and sow peace in the minds of men through the abundance of your powers.
I will stay with you from now on as your comfort, and I will keep you in peace with steadfast strength in every place."
Then suddenly a sound was heard, loud in the air. A host of heaven's angels, a beautiful troop, messengers of glory, came in a throng.
Our King went up through the roof of the temple while they watched, the chosen thegns who were still following in the footsteps of the beloved one at that meeting-place.

They saw their Lord, the Son of God, rise up from the earth on high. Their spirits were sad, burning in their hearts, their minds mourning, because they could no longer see one so dear to them under the sky.
Heavenly messengers raised a song. They praised the Prince, lauded the Author of life, and rejoiced in the light that shone from the Saviour's head.
They saw two all-bright angels shining beautifully in their adornments around the First-born, the glory of kings.
With wondrous words and a bright voice the angels called down from on high over the crowd of men: "Why are you waiting, men of Galilee, standing in a circle?

"Now you clearly see the true Lord go into the sky. The possessor of victory, the foremost of princes, the creator of all peoples, will ascend from here to his homeland with this band of angels, to the Father's native throne."

With this company we will bring the Lord over the vaults of the heavens to the bright city, with this joyful band. He is the best and noblest of all the children of victory, the one you are gazing at here and see with joy, shining in his adornments.
Yet he will come again himself to seek out the nations of the earth with a vast host, and then he will judge every deed that the peoples under the heavens have done."

Then the Guardian of glory, the King of archangels, the protector of the saints, was surrounded by clouds, up above the roofs. Hope was renewed, and joy in the cities, through the coming of that hero.
Triumphant, the eternal Author of blessedness sat down at the right hand of his own Father.
Then the brave-hearted men went to Jerusalem, into the holy city, sad at heart, from the place where they had last seen God, their giver of joy, rising up before their eyes.
There was a ring of weeping, overwhelmed with grief; true love was hot at the heart, the breast welled up within, the mind in the man's breast burned.

All the glorious thegns waited there for the lord's promise in the bright city ten nights more, as the possessor of heaven himself had commanded them, before the ruler of all ascended into the protection of the heavens. Shining angels came to meet the giver of blessings to men.
That is well said, as the writings tell, that all-bright angels came to meet him in troops at that holy time, descending through the sky.
Then the greatest of feasts took place in glory. It was very fitting that thegns, brightly clothed, a beautiful troop, came to that joy in the prince's city.
The welcome ones saw on the high throne the ruler of heaven, the life-giver of peoples, ruler in splendour of all middle-earth and of the majestic host.
"The holy one has now plundered hell of all the tribute that it unjustly swallowed in that war in days of old.
Now the champions of the devils are overcome, humiliated and bound in living torment, in the abyss of hell, stripped of glory.
The adversaries could not succeed in battle with the casting of weapons, since the king of glory, the protector of the heavenly kingdom, waged war against his ancient enemies by his own might alone,
when he led out of captivity the greatest of plunder from the city of fiends, a countless multitude of people, this same throng that you gaze upon here.
Now the Saviour of souls, God's own Son, will seek the gift-throne of spirits, after the battle-play.
Now you know well who the lord is who leads this host; now go boldly and glad-hearted to meet your friends. Gates, open!

The ruler of all, the king, the creator of works of old, wishes to lead into you, into the city, with no small company, the people whom he took from the devils through his own victory, into the joy of joys.
Peace shall be shared between angels and men from now on, forever and for all time. There is a covenant between God and men together: holy faith, love, the hope of life, and the joy of all light."
Lo, we have now heard how the child of salvation through his coming here gave back salvation, freed and protected the people under the skies, the glorious son of the Creator,
so that now every man, while he lives here, may choose either the humiliation of hell or the glory of heaven, either the bright light or the hateful night,
either the force of majesty or the exile of darkness, either joy with the Lord or clamour with the devils, either torment among the wrathful or glory among the honoured, either life or death,
whichever he prefers to bring about, while flesh and spirit dwell in the world. For that may the majesty of the Trinity have glory, thanks without end!
It is fitting that the nations of men should give thanks to the Lord for every benefit that he has always done for us, late and early, through the mystery of manifold powers.

He gives us food and abundance of possessions, wealth across the wide land, and mild weather under the shelter of the sky. Sun and moon, noblest of stars, candles of heaven, shine for all people on earth.
Dew and rain fall and call forth good things as sustenance for the race of men; they increase the riches of the earth.
For all this we must give thanks and praise to our Lord, and above all for the salvation that he gave us as our hope,
Then at his ascension he reversed the misery that we had endured before, and the only-begotten king settled for the dwellers on earth the greatest of feuds with the beloved Father.
Afterwards the decree was turned to peace for souls, the decree that had earlier been pronounced in an angry mind, to the sorrow of men:
"I made you upon the earth. On it you must live in miseries, dwell in strife and endure exile and suffering, and sing a death-song to the delight of enemies,
and you must return to that same earth, swarming with worms. From there, out of that earth, you must afterwards go to the fire of torment."
Lo, the prince made this easier for us when he took on limbs and a body, a man's offspring!
When the son of the Creator, the God of hosts, wished to ascend to the homeland of the angels, that longed-for gift came to us, the lowly, as help in that holy time.

Concerning this Job, as well as he knew how, composed a song: he praised the protector of men, glorified the Saviour, and with kinship-love gave the Son of the Ruler a friendly name and called him a bird, which the Jews could not understand in the divine strength of the spirit.
The flight of the bird was hidden and secret from enemies on earth, those who had a dark understanding in their breasts, a stony heart.
They would not acknowledge the bright signs, many and various, which the noble Son of God performed before them throughout the world.

So the beloved bird tried its flight: at times, brave and strong in powers, he sought up the dwelling of the angels, the greater home; at times he darted back to earth, sought the surface of the ground through the grace of the Spirit, and turned to the world.
Concerning this the prophet sang: "He was raised up in the embrace of angels in the abundance of his great powers, high and holy, above the majesty of the heavens."

Those who denied the ascension could not recognize the flight of the bird, and did not believe that the Author of life, holy, in human form, was raised up from the earth above the majesty of the hosts.
Then he who made this world, God's spiritual Son, honoured us and gave us gifts, eternal dwellings above with the angels, and also sowed and set manifold wisdom of mind throughout the minds of men.

To one he sends wise eloquence into the thought of his mind through the spirit of his mouth, noble understanding. He to whom the skill of wisdom is entrusted in his heart can sing and tell a great many things.
One can stir the harp loudly with his fingers before men, play upon the wood of music. One can rightly expound the divine law. One can tell the course of the stars, the wide creation.
One can skilfully write words. To one he grants success in war, in battle, when the shooters send the spear-throng over the shield-cover, flickering arrow-work.
One can boldly drive a ship over the salt sea, stir up the force of the ocean. One can climb the high, steep tree.
One can make a steeled sword, a weapon. One knows the course of the plains, the far-reaching roads. So the Ruler, God's Son on earth, deals out his gifts to us.
He will not give all the wisdom of the spirit to any one person alone, lest pride harm him, because his skill alone set him above others.
Thus mighty God, King of all creatures, with ungrudging gifts honours the offspring of the earth with skills;
likewise he grants glory to the blessed in heaven and establishes peace for ever and ever for angels and men; so he honours his work.
Of this the prophet said that holy jewels were raised up high, bright stars of heaven, the sun and the moon. What are those jewels, so shining, but God himself?
He is the true beam of the sun, a noble radiance to angels and to the dwellers on earth.
The moon shines over the world, a spiritual star; so God's church shines brightly through the gathering together of truth and righteousness.
As it says in books, after God's Son, King of everything pure, ascended from the earth, the church here endured persecution by lawbreakers under the power of heathen shepherds.
There the sinful enemies paid no heed to truth or to the spirit's need, but they broke and burned God's temple, shed blood, hated and struck down.
Yet through the gift of the Spirit the glory of God's thegns came forth after the ascension of the eternal Lord.
Concerning this Solomon sang, the son of David, ruler of nations, ready-wise in songs and in spiritual mysteries, and spoke this word:

"It will become known that the King of angels, the Lord strong in powers, will leap upon the mountain, will spring over the high hills, will cover the hills and knolls with his glory, and will redeem the world, all the dwellers on earth, through that noble leap."
The first leap was when he came down into a woman, a spotless maiden, and there took on human form without sin, which became a comfort to all who dwell on earth.
The second leap was the birth of the child, when he, the majesty of all majesties, lay in the manger in the form of a child, wrapped in cloths.
The third leap, the rush of the King of heaven, was when he climbed onto the cross, Father, Spirit of comfort. The fourth leap was into the tomb, when he gave up the tree, fast in the earthen house.

The fifth leap was when he humbled the host of hell's inhabitants in living torment, and bound within it their king, the spokesman of the fiends, the hostile-minded one, with fiery fetters, where he still lies in prison, fastened in chains, bound by his sins.
The sixth leap, the joyful play of the Holy One, was when he ascended to heaven, to his former home. Then the throng of angels at that holy time became glad with laughter and joys.
They saw the majesty of glory, the chief of princes, come to visit his homeland, the bright dwellings. Then the prince's play became eternal joy to the blessed citizens.
Thus here on earth the eternal Son of God leapt in bounds over the high slopes, bold across the mountains.

So we men must, with the thoughts of our hearts, leap by leaps from strength to strength and strive for glories, so that by holy works we may climb to the highest roof, where there is hope and bliss, a splendid band of thanes.
We have great need to seek salvation with our hearts, where in spirit we eagerly believe that the Child of salvation, the living God, ascended up from here with our body.
Therefore we must always scorn idle desires and sin-wounds, and rejoice in what is better.
For our comfort we have the almighty Father in the heavens. He sends his messengers here from there, holy ones from on high, who shield us against the grievous arrow-flights of the destroyers,
so that the hostile ones may not inflict wounds when the bringer of strife shoots a bitter arrow from his crafty bow into God's people.

Therefore we must always keep a firm and wary watch against the sudden shot, so that the poisoned point, the bitter missile, the sudden trap of the fiends, may not pierce in under the body's bone-house. That is a dangerous wound, the palest of wounds.

Let us protect ourselves, then, while we live in our home on earth. Let us seek peace from the Father, and pray to the Son of God and the gracious Spirit that he shield us against the weapons of the foe,
against the lying snares of the hateful ones, he who gave us life, limbs, body and spirit. Praise be to him always, forever and ever, and glory in the heavens.
No one of the race of men on earth need fear the devils' arrows, the spear-attack of the fierce ones, if God, Lord of hosts, shields him.
The judgment is near, when we shall receive rewards matching what we have gathered by our works throughout our lives across the wide earth.
Books tell us how at the first the humble one, the gold-hoard of powers, the noble Son of God, holy from on high, came down into middle-earth, into the virgin's womb.
Indeed, I expect and also dread a harsher judgment for myself when the Prince of angels comes again, because I have not kept well what my Saviour commanded me in books.
I must see the terror of that, the punishment of sin, as I truly reckon, where many will be led to the assembly before the face of the eternal Judge.

Then C [rune ᚳ: cen 'torch', or perhaps 'the bold one'? [?]] will tremble; he will hear the King speak, the Ruler of the heavens, speak harsh words to those who formerly obeyed him poorly in the world, while Y [rune ᚣ: yr? [?]] and N [rune ᚾ: nyd 'need'? [?]] could most easily find comfort.
There many a one, frightened and weary, must wait in that place for what fierce punishments he will decree for him according to his deeds.
W [rune ᚹ: wyn 'joy'] of the earth's adornments will be gone. U [rune ᚢ: ur 'our'?] share of life's joys, F [rune ᚠ: feoh 'wealth'] on earth, was long enclosed by L [rune ᛚ: lagu 'water'] by floods.
Then the adornments must burn in the fire; the bright, swift red flame will rage, will stride fiercely across the wide world. The plains will fall, the cities will burst apart.
The fire will be on the move; the greediest of spirits will burn up without pity the ancient treasures that men once held, while they had pride on earth.

Therefore I wish to teach every beloved one not to neglect the need of his spirit, nor pour it out in vainglory, while God wills that he may dwell here in the world, the soul journeying together with the body in that spirit's guest-house.
Every man ought in his days on earth to consider earnestly that the Ruler of powers came to us mildly at the first, through the word of the angel.
It will be a serious matter when he comes again, fierce and righteous. The sky will be shaken, and the great expanses of the world will tremble then.

The bright King will repay them for having lived on earth by wicked deeds, stained with sins. For that, weary in spirit, they must long receive a terrible requital in the bath of fire, driven about by its surges, when the King of powers, greatest of majesties, comes to the assembly.
The terror of the people will be heard loudly with the noise of heaven, the cry of the mourners; those who trust weakly in their works will weep with anxiety before the face of the eternal Judge.

There will be revealed a terror greater than was ever heard of on earth since the first creation. There, in that swift hour, it will be far dearer to each of the sinners than all this fleeting creation, [?]
where he may hide himself in that victorious host, when the Lord of hosts, the chief of princes, judges all, the loved and the hated, giving reward according to right to every nation.
We have great need to think earnestly about the beauty of the soul in this barren time, before that terror and dread.
Now it is most like this: as if we were sailing in ships on the flood, over cold water, across the wide sea, travelling on sea-horses, on flood-wood.

That stream on which we toss here is perilous, waves beyond measure, windy seas over the deep way, throughout this feeble world. Our life was hard before we had sailed to land over the rough ridge of the sea.

Then help came to us, which led us to the harbour of salvation: God's spiritual Son. He gave us grace so that we may know, over the ship's side, where we must tie up our sea-horses, our old wave-steeds, made fast with anchors.
Let us fix our hope on that harbour which the Ruler of the heavens, holy on high, opened for us when he ascended into heaven.
